title: Logical Equivalence and the Law List
quickIdea: Two formulas are logically equivalent when they agree in every row. A small list of laws rewrites almost any GATE expression without a truth table.
remember: Identity: p and T = p; p or F = p. Domination: p or T = T; p and F = F.
Idempotent: p or p = p; p and p = p. Double negation: not not p = p.
Commutative and associative laws hold for and, or, xor - not for implies.
Distributive: p and (q or r) = (p and q) or (p and r); p or (q and r) = (p or q) and (p or r).
De Morgan: not (p and q) = not p or not q; not (p or q) = not p and not q.
Absorption: p or (p and q) = p; p and (p or q) = p.
Implication: p -> q = not p or q. Contrapositive: p -> q = not q -> not p. Exportation: (p and q) -> r = p -> (q -> r).
Biconditional: p <-> q = (p -> q) and (q -> p) = (p and q) or (not p and not q). Negation of biconditional: not (p <-> q) = p xor q.

example.work: p -> q = not p or q, so not (p -> q) = not (not p or q) = p and not q by De Morgan.
example.answer: p and not q - 'p happens and q does not'.

gateAngle: GATE 2015 Set 1 Q.14 asks which formula is NOT equivalent to p <-> q. Three options are rewrites of the biconditional; the odd one, (not p and q) or (p and not q), is p xor q, its negation. Equivalence questions are answered by rewriting, not by eight rows.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Simplify not (not p and q) or (p and q).
variations.why: De Morgan turns not (not p and q) into p or not q. The whole expression becomes (p or not q) or (p and q); by absorption the (p and q) term adds nothing, leaving p or not q.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Is p -> (q -> r) equivalent to (p -> q) -> r?
variations.why: At p = false, q = false, r = false the left side is false -> (false -> false) = false -> true = true, while the right side is (false -> false) -> false = true -> false = false. Implication is not associative.

trap.what: Pushing a negation through a bracket without flipping the connective, and assuming implication is associative.
trap.why: De Morgan flips AND to OR and OR to AND. Distributing a negation like a multiplier gives a wrong formula in most rows.
trap.counterexample: not (p and q) is not equal to not p and not q. At p = true, q = false the left side is true and the right side is false.

check.question: Rewrite p -> q using only not and or.
check.explanation: These two agree in all four rows: both are false only when p is true and q is false.
